text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High error rate (502/504) and elevated p99 latency for hosted API and Dedicated pools in Dublin (eu-west-1). Alerting rule: api.gateway.5xx_rate > 5% over 1m. Triggered at 2024-05-05T08:15:12Z

sara (oncall): I'm on it. seeing spike in 502/504 from upstream auth proxy. hitting timeouts to identity provider.

kevin (eng-sre): Confirmed. The auth-proxy service in eu-west-1 is logging a flurry of `upstream timeout` and `502` when calling token-introspect endpoint. Third-party vendor (Okta) shows degraded in eu-west-1 on their status page.

lia (runtime): This is impacting both hosted API frontends and dedicated pools because the request flow does a per-request token introspect for customer tokens. When auth-proxy blocks, request pipeline times out and surfaces 5xx.

maria (support): We're starting to get customer reports: two mid-market users seeing repeated 502s for inference calls. CS has notified them we're investigating. Any quick mitigation?

kevin (eng-sre): Short term mitigations we can try: 1) enable locally-cached token allowlist to bypass introspect for recently-seen tokens, 2) increase auth-proxy timeouts to avoid cascading, 3) route auth-proxy for new requests to other regions where possible. I'll prep PR for (1) and (2) and coordinate with routing.

sara (oncall): Agree. Priorities: minimize customer impact, preserve safety. Lia, can your team flip cache-bypass to allow up to 30s TTL on verified tokens? Need emergency config change.

lia (runtime): I can roll a config change to auth-proxy: set `token_cache_ttl=30s` and `introspect_timeout=250ms` in eu-west-1. That will reduce outbound pressure and failfast when needed. Rolling now as a canary to 2 frontends.

opsbot: Deploy started: auth-proxy config patch => env=eu-west-1 => canary pods: 2/2.

kevin (eng-sre): Also pushing a routing tweak: mark eu-west-1 auth-proxy as degraded in service registry so cross-region calls from hosted API can try eu-west-2 fallback for introspect. This will add a small latency for token checks but avoid timeouts.

zane (eng-platform): I'm enabling fallback routing for auth-proxy from host frontends: prefer eu-west-1, fallback eu-west-2 after 100ms. Pushing now.

sara (oncall): Maria, update customers that we've identified Okta partial outage in eu-west-1 causing token introspect failures; we've applied cache fallback and cross-region routing to reduce 5xx. We're still monitoring.

maria (support): Sending templated update to affected customers now.

kevin (eng-sre): Quick telemetry: before changes 5xx_rate=8.7%, p99=2.4s. After canary config and routing (5m): 5xx_rate=2.1%, p99=480ms. Still seeing intermittent 502s for long-lived tokens that hit fresh introspect requests.

sara (oncall): Good improvement. Keep watch for side effects. Lia, any regression risk from allowing cached tokens TTL=30s?

lia (runtime): Slightly increased window for stale token acceptance but our cached entries include expiry checks based on token exp claim. We won't accept expired tokens. This is opt-in emergency behavior and limited to eu-west-1 frontends. I'll add an audit log flag to track bypassed-introspects.

kevin (eng-sre): Noted. Also enabling a temporary rate limit on auth-proxy -> Okta to avoid hammering them while degraded.

incident-bot: Note: oncall handoff scheduled in 55 minutes. Pager rotation: sara -> kevin.

sara (oncall): I'll create an incident incident-doc and pass to next oncall. High-level summary: Okta partial outage in eu-west-1 caused token introspect failures; auth-proxy timeouts caused 502/504 in hosted API and Dedicated customer pools. Mitigations: enabled token cache TTL, reduced introspect timeout, enabled cross-region fallback routing, rate-limited auth-proxy outgoing calls. Customer impact: intermittent 5xx and elevated tail latency for ~20% of requests in eu-west-1 for ~35 minutes. Next steps: revert emergency config when Okta confirms recovery, add circuit breaker to auth-proxy, implement persistent token caching layer with consented TTL.

zane (eng-platform): I'll file a follow-up ticket to add persistent cache with eviction and signed-caching semantics. tag: INF-4172.

maria (support): Logged affected customers and ticket numbers. Will coordinate SLA credit eval if customers escalate.

kevin (eng-sre): Okta status showing partial recovery in eu-west-1. We should start rolling back emergency TTL in 10m and monitor.

lia (runtime): Rolling config rollback to normal TTL=5s and introspect_timeout=500ms in canary now, will monitor for errors while Okta finishes recovery.

opsbot: Deploy started: auth-proxy rollback => env=eu-west-1 => canary pods: 2/2.

kevin (eng-sre): Post-rollback metrics (10m window): 5xx_rate=0.4%, p99=180ms. Looks healthy.

sara (oncall): OK, I'm closing the paging alert as mitigations applied and upstream recovered. I'll hand off to zane for follow-up engineering work and to maria for customer follow-ups.

maria (support): Acknowledged. Sending final customer updates and scheduling possible SLA review with finance if impacted >1h.

zane (eng-platform): I'll own INF-4172 and pair with runtime on the caching design. Action items: design doc due EOD, PR in 3 days.

incident-bot: Incident closed by sara at 2024-05-05T09:06:40Z :white_check_mark:

sara (oncall): Thanks team. Postmortem to follow.

kevin (eng-sre): Note for postmortem: consider decoupling hard dependency on real-time introspect for high-throughput inference paths; add circuit-breakers and regional async verification mechanism.

lia (runtime): Adding logs for any future bypassed-introspects to aid audits.

maria (support): Filing customer impact summary for postmortem attachment.
